haiku-low.q1: Keys load at process start, before the HTTP server comes up; readiness cannot pass until loading finishes.
haiku-low.q2: It retries the full load three times (2 s apart), then exits non-zero and never goes ready. The rollout halts; old replicas keep serving.
haiku-low.q3: Re-reads all three every 5 minutes, swapping changed entries atomically. On failure it keeps the last good value, warns (name and error), retries next tick.
haiku-low.q4: In-memory, per-process SecretCache dict only. Values must never go to disk, env vars, or logs; version ids may be logged.
haiku-low.q5: The prod replicas' identity orders-api-prod reads orders-api/prod/* read-only. Only security on-call writes prod; engineers have no prod access.
haiku-low.q6: Old keys remain in git history, so deletion alone is insufficient. Rotating at each vendor and revoking the old key makes them useless.
haiku-low.q7: Each client calls secrets.get(name) on every outgoing vendor call and puts it in the Authorization header; refreshed keys apply from the next request.
haiku-low.q8: Each replica's /healthz secret_versions must show the new version id; all four must match before security on-call revokes the old key.
haiku-low.q9: Store access, then copying keys into the store, then one merge switching the app to the store and removing keys from app.yaml, then provider rotation.
haiku-low.q10: From the orders-api/dev/* path (APP_ENV=dev set by make run), using the developer's own login; sandbox keys, not live keys.
haiku-low.q11: It never starts on a partial set: it retries the whole load three times, then logs names and exits non-zero.
haiku-low.q12: No. The plan does only a one-time rotation; Security has not decided on a regular schedule.

sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded first, at process start in main before the HTTP server comes up; readiness (GET /healthz) can't pass until the load is done.
sonnet.q2: It retries the whole load 3 times with 2 s between tries, then logs names (not values) and exits non-zero, so it never goes ready. Because deploys roll one pod at a time (maxUnavailable 0) and a new pod must pass /healthz before an old one stops, the rollout halts while the old replicas keep serving traffic.
sonnet.q3: A background refresher runs every 5 minutes after startup, re-reads all three, and when a version id changes swaps that entry atomically as one assignment (logging '<name> now at version <id>'). If the read fails (whole vault or one name), it keeps the last good value for what couldn't be read, updates the ones that could, warns (name + error only), and retries next tick without exiting or going unready.
sonnet.q4: Held in an in-process, per-process in-memory dict of name -> (value, version id). They must never go to disk, env vars, or logs (version ids may be logged).
sonnet.q5: Read: orders-api-prod identity (the 4 prod replicas), read-only on orders-api/prod/*; security on-call also (it writes). Write: only security on-call. Engineers have no access to prod.
sonnet.q6: The old keys have been in git history for two years and history won't be rewritten, so removing them from the file doesn't make them secret. Rotating them at each vendor (new key in vault, then old key revoked at the vendor) is what makes the old values useless/harmless.
sonnet.q7: The clients call secrets.get(name) on every outgoing vendor call and put the result in the Authorization header, instead of copying the key in __init__; so a refreshed key is used from the next request, no restart, and the map is the only copy.
sonnet.q8: Wait about 10 minutes (refresh every 5 min), then check the health endpoint (/healthz secret_versions) on every replica, all 4 must show the new version id; only then does security on-call revoke the old key at the vendor. If a replica is stuck, don't revoke; check logs or restart it.
sonnet.q9: 1) Set store access/permissions (and test them); 2) copy keys into the store (prod values and dev sandbox keys); 3) one merge switches the app to read from the store and removes the api_key lines from config/app.yaml (same change), triggering the rolling deploy; 4) verify all four instances on the first versions; 5) then rotate keys at the providers (step 1), one vendor at a time.
sonnet.q10: From the dev path orders-api/dev/* in the secret store (sandbox keys), via make run setting APP_ENV=dev, using the developer's own login.
sonnet.q11: It never starts on a partial set. It retries the whole load three times, 2 s apart, then logs the names (not values) and exits with a non-zero code, so the pod never goes ready.
sonnet.q12: Not decided. Security hasn't decided whether there is a regular rotation schedule or how often; this plan only does the one-time rotation.
